text: The autoscaling floor and the bucket policy look unrelated, but they share one root cause: both pull requests passed their checks because nothing actually looked at what the change would do.

The guardrail adds one step to Lesson Five's pipeline: terraform show, dash json, turning the plan into structured data a script can actually inspect, right alongside the existing plan-as-comment step.

One check flags any minReplicas value above four, unless the pull request carries a deliberate peak-season-override label. A second check scans every S3 bucket policy for a wildcard Principal with no Condition attached.
Both checks fail loudly: a non-zero exit code fails the job, and branch protection makes that failure actually block the merge button, with a clear comment explaining exactly which rule tripped.
Neither original mistake took unusual skill to make. That's exactly why the check belongs in the pipeline, which doesn't get tired or distracted, instead of in a checklist someone has to remember.
